tools.title: Observable as a lazy push collection
tools.definition: The one core type: a lazily evaluated computation that, once subscribed, pushes zero to many values, synchronously or asynchronously, until a single error or completion; nothing runs before subscribe.

tools.title: Unhandled errors and producer interference

transform.reason: Error propagation through producers requires an exception and handler model.

observable: Candidate traces show whether a receiver failure interrupts other deliveries.

tools.definition: An error with no consumer handler is reported through the library's unhandled-error path; an error allowed to unwind the stack through a producer's notification loop can break upstream iteration. Doctrine: handle errors where they occur, never let them unwind through producers.

tools.title: Result type (errors as values)

transform.reason: Converting errors into tagged values requires an application result schema.

observable: Candidate traces show recoverable failures as data followed by later results.

tools.definition: Map inner results to {ok: true, value} | {ok: false, error} with catchError inside the inner stream; the outer stream never errors, consumers branch on the tag, and effects translate the two cases to success/failure actions.

tools.title: webSocket subject
tools.definition: webSocket({url, openObserver, closeObserver, serializer, deserializer}) returns a Subject: next() sends, subscribing receives; deserializer defaults to JSON.parse; openObserver/closeObserver observe lifecycle; multiplex(sub, unsub, filter) shares one socket across logical channels.

tools.title: WebSocket reconnection

transform.reason: Reconnection requires connection sessions, resubscription messages and replay safety.

observable: Candidate traces show dropped sessions, delayed reconnects and rejoined consumers.

tools.definition: Problem: survive drops. Shape: socket$.pipe(retry({delay: backoff}), repeat({delay})) so errors and normal closes both resubscribe, which reconnects; openObserver re-sends subscriptions. Fails when: messages sent while disconnected are lost (buffer and flush on open), or when reconnect storms lack jitter.

hooks.clause: the resident has no network transport (a fresh loopback connection per request), so this applies only if a push channel is added

verified.note: RX-SRC retry, repeat; composition MK; DOTLN

tools.title: Streaming resources (SSE, sockets) into signals

transform.reason: A streaming resource needs a host signal model, status schema and stream factory.

observable: Candidate views show multiple source values updating one resource.

tools.definition: Angular's resource accepts a stream factory for sources that emit many values; rxResource takes an observable stream and must emit a value or error before completing.

tools.title: Route params as streams

transform.reason: Route parameter schemas and parameter-driven loading are unspecified.

observable: Candidate traces show route changes producing replacement data requests.

tools.definition: Problem: a reused component must react to parameter changes. Shape: route.paramMap.pipe(map(p => p.get('id')), switchMap(load)); ActivatedRoute's url, params, queryParams, fragment, data, paramMap, queryParamMap and title are observables that emit on shallow change. Fails when: snapshot is used in a reused component (misses changes) or a deep change inside resolved data does not emit.

tools.title: Animation with animationFrameScheduler

transform.reason: Browser repaint timing and rendering work need execution contexts outside the toy enum.

observable: Candidate timelines align visual updates with repaint opportunities.

tools.definition: Problem: smooth per-frame updates. Shape: interval(0, animationFrameScheduler) or observeOn(animationFrameScheduler) schedules work just before the next repaint. Fails when: a delay is passed (falls back to async timing), when frames queue while the tab is hidden, or when heavy work runs inside the frame.

hooks.clause: BoardFacade's afterNextRender plus requestAnimationFrame focus step is the imperative form

tools.title: DOM events as streams

transform.reason: Adapting event listeners requires an external event API and teardown ownership.

observable: Candidate traces show listeners appearing and disappearing with consumers.

tools.definition: fromEvent(target, type) wraps add/removeEventListener with teardown; fromEventPattern adapts other handler APIs; composition replaces manual listener bookkeeping.

tools.title: Game loop

transform.reason: A frame-driven simulation needs a state model, input interpretation and transition function.

observable: Candidate traces show state advancing once per frame using current input.

tools.definition: A frame stream drives state with expand/scan, bufferCount pairs frames, withLatestFrom reads input state; the archetype for simulation ticks.

tools.title: Stop watch

transform.reason: A stopwatch requires control states, counter arithmetic and timer creation.

observable: Candidate traces show elapsed ticks pausing and resetting.

tools.definition: Controls (start, stop, reset) switchMap into interval or NEVER; scan accumulates ticks; startWith seeds the display.

tools.title: Smart counter

transform.reason: Numeric animation requires interpolation and stopping rules; a number target is not a spatial objective.

observable: Candidate traces show a displayed number approaching its requested value.

tools.definition: Animate a number toward a target: a Subject of targets switchMaps into timer ticks, scan steps the value, takeWhile stops at the target.

tools.title: Lodash for events
tools.definition: The library's own framing: operators are pure functions over collections of events, so state that would otherwise live in shared variables lives inside the pipeline.

tools.title: Progress bar
tools.definition: Several requests complete over time; count or scan the completions against the total and render a percentage; share the request stream so counting does not refetch.

tools.title: HTTP polling (recipe)

transform.reason: Polling creates repeated requests and needs a source plus a chosen cadence and stop rule.

observable: Candidate timelines show request attempts ending at the stop condition.

tools.definition: Two forms are shown: interval/timer with switchMap, and a request repeated with delay plus a stop condition via takeUntil or filter.

tools.title: Lockscreen pattern gesture

transform.reason: Pad geometry, gesture decoding and attempt validation require a gesture model.

observable: Candidate traces show a completed pointer path converted into one attempt.

tools.definition: Pointer down starts a trace; moves are throttled and mapped to pads; up completes the attempt (toArray) and repeat re-arms.

tools.title: Horizontal scroll indicator

transform.reason: Scroll geometry and display width mapping are rendering operations outside the enum.

observable: Candidate views compare scroll position with a displayed percentage.

tools.definition: Scroll events throttled and mapped to a percentage width; the simplest audit/throttle UI case.

tools.title: Error is terminal
tools.definition: An error notification ends the subscription and finalizes the producer; no value follows it. Every error strategy is therefore a decision about which stream is allowed to die.

tools.title: Error channel vs error value

transform.reason: Choosing terminal failure versus a failure payload needs error and value schemas.

observable: Candidate traces compare continued values with termination after a failure.

tools.definition: The error channel is for failures that should end the stream; failures the UI must display and recover from belong in the value channel as data (result types, status unions). Choosing the channel decides whether consumers keep receiving later values.

hooks.clause: H2's known/unknown/unavailable are value-channel failures; a stream that errors cannot show them

tools.title: Notification objects (materialize/dematerialize)

transform.reason: Encoding and decoding notification payloads is not message delivery or routing policy.

observable: Candidate traces compare terminal signals with equivalent tagged values.

tools.definition: materialize wraps next, error and complete as Notification values so failures can be inspected, counted or folded; dematerialize restores them.

tools.title: Errors must be Error instances

transform.reason: Requiring structured error instances is a payload type and code-validation rule.

observable: Candidate inspection distinguishes structured failures from untyped payloads.

tools.definition: Error notifications should carry Error values (stack, message, type) rather than strings or objects; lint throw-error enforces this for throwError and Subject.error.

tools.title: catchError inside the inner flattening

transform.reason: Inner versus outer recovery needs a nested subscription graph and fallback payload.

observable: Candidate traces show later triggers surviving one failed inner operation.

tools.definition: Problem: one failed request kills a long-lived stream. Shape: outer$.pipe(switchMap(x => inner(x).pipe(catchError(err => of(fallback))))) catches per inner so the outer keeps listening. Fails when: catchError is placed on the outer (the outer completes after the fallback and stops reacting), or the fallback hides the failure from the user.

verified.note: NGRX-FX (catchError inside the inner observable); ESL (no-unsafe-catch)

tools.title: catchError → EMPTY vs fallback value

transform.reason: Silent completion, failure values and rethrowing require separate error contracts.

observable: Candidate traces compare visible failure information and stream termination.

tools.definition: Returning EMPTY swallows the failure and completes the inner silently (fine for optional side streams); returning of(failureAction) or a status value surfaces it; rethrowing (throwError) delegates to an outer handler. NgRx's own examples show both EMPTY and a failure action.

tools.title: Marble thinking

transform.reason: A time diagram is a reasoning view rather than an enum-backed scene transformation.

observable: Candidate timelines display emissions and terminal events.

tools.definition: Reason about a stream as a line of time carrying values, a completion bar and an error mark; the same picture serves documentation, whiteboards and ASCII marble tests.

tools.title: Unsafe catchError in effects (no-unsafe-catch)

transform.reason: Correct recovery placement depends on effect lifetime and nested subscription ownership.

observable: Candidate traces show whether a failed operation ends the whole effect.

tools.definition: A catchError on the effect's outer stream that returns a value completes the effect; the lint rule flags catches that are not inside the flattening operator.

tools.title: Effects resubscribe-on-error safety net
tools.definition: When an effect's main stream errors, NgRx reports to ErrorHandler and resubscribes (up to 10 times) so the app keeps reacting to actions; it is a safety net, not a strategy: operators like startWith re-run on each resubscription, and handled effects can opt out with useEffectsErrorHandler: false.

tools.title: tapResponse

transform.reason: Notification callbacks can run arbitrary state and cleanup effects not specified here.

observable: Candidate traces show handled results and failures without terminating the parent flow.

tools.definition: NgRx's operator for inner streams: handle next and error (and finalize) without letting the error escape; the standard body of rxMethod and ComponentStore effects.

tools.title: Service rethrow, consumer decides

transform.reason: Service versus consumer error responsibility is an ownership boundary requiring handlers.

observable: Candidate traces show one failure reaching independently chosen consumer fallbacks.

tools.definition: A service's data stream logs (tap/catchError) and rethrows so each consumer decides its own fallback; silent catches in services hide failures from every screen at once.

tools.title: finalize for cleanup regardless of outcome

transform.reason: Arbitrary cleanup callbacks require resource identities and an ownership lifecycle.

observable: Candidate traces show one resource release for every termination path.

tools.definition: finalize(callback) runs once on complete, error or unsubscribe; use it for loading flags, spinners and releasing resources, never for business logic that must know the outcome.

tools.title: retry(count) and retry with delay

transform.reason: Resubscribing an arbitrary source needs source execution, error and replay-safety semantics.

observable: Candidate traces show bounded repeated attempts after failure.

tools.definition: retry({count, delay, resetOnSuccess}) resubscribes the source on error; delay as a number waits, delay as a function returns a notifier whose emission retries, whose completion ends quietly and whose error propagates; resetOnSuccess restarts the count after a successful value.

tools.title: Retry only what is transient

transform.reason: Transient and permanent failure classes require a domain-specific error taxonomy.

observable: Candidate traces show permanent failures ending attempts immediately.

tools.definition: Classify errors before retrying: network and 5xx transient, 4xx and validation permanent; implement by rethrowing permanent errors from the delay function so retry gives up at once.

tools.title: repeat as the success-side twin
tools.definition: repeat({count, delay}) resubscribes after completion the way retry does after error; polling after a completed request is repeat, not retry.

tools.title: retryWhen/repeatWhen → retry/repeat with delay
tools.definition: The notifier-based forms are superseded by config objects; lint no-ignored-notifier catches notifier functions that ignore their input, the classic infinite-retry bug.

tools.title: Timeout as an error source
tools.definition: timeout raises TimeoutError (with optional meta for identification) or switches to a fallback via `with`; treat it as one more transient error class in the retry policy.

tools.title: Ask: what is the shape of the stream in time?

transform.reason: Shape questions describe requirements but do not select a concrete runtime policy.

observable: Candidate timelines expose count, timing, termination and overlap.

tools.definition: Before picking operators, name cardinality (0, 1, many), termination (finite, endless), timing (sync, async, bursty) and overlap (may inner work overlap or must it cancel, queue or be ignored); the official decision tree is organised by exactly these questions.

hooks.clause: for each console surface name whether it is a value over time (signal) or events over time (stream) before choosing the primitive

tools.title: Share and error state

transform.reason: Error reset changes shared producer state, beyond a channel delivery policy.

observable: Candidate traces show whether later receivers restart a failed source.

tools.definition: A shared stream that errors stays errored unless resetOnError is true (the default for share); shareReplay replays the error to late subscribers; decide the reset behaviour when sharing anything that can fail.

tools.title: no-ignored-error

transform.reason: Installing error handling requires a handler and exception reporting contract.

observable: Candidate inspection finds consumers with no failure path.

tools.definition: subscribe without an error handler lets failures surface as unhandled errors; the rule requires an error callback or an upstream catchError.

tools.title: no-implicit-any-catch
tools.definition: catchError, subscribe and tap error parameters must be typed unknown and narrowed, mirroring the TypeScript catch-clause rule.

tools.title: no-redundant-notify

transform.reason: Detecting redundant sends requires notification lifecycle and code-validation semantics.

observable: Candidate traces identify attempted notifications after closure.

tools.definition: Do not call next, error or complete on a subject that has already errored or completed; the notification is silently dropped and signals a logic bug.

tools.title: no-async-subscribe

transform.reason: Unobserved promise failures require async task ownership and error propagation rules.

observable: Candidate traces show whether asynchronous callback rejection is observed.

tools.definition: An async function passed to subscribe returns a promise nobody observes, so rejections are lost and ordering is unclear; flatten with mergeMap/concatMap over from(promise) instead.

tools.title: Compose completion instead of collecting subscriptions

transform.reason: Composed completion needs a subscription graph and resource cleanup model.

observable: Candidate views compare one completion path with individually owned cancellations.

tools.definition: Lesh's doctrine: rather than storing Subscription objects and unsubscribing each, build streams whose completion is composed in (takeUntil(destroy$), take, first, takeWhile); completion is a notification you can react to, unsubscribe is not.

tools.title: takeUntil(destroy$) pattern

transform.reason: Destruction notifiers require a component owner and nested subscription lifecycle.

observable: Candidate traces show all owned streams stopping when the owner ends.

tools.definition: Problem: component-scoped streams must end on destroy. Shape: a private destroy$ Subject<void>; every pipe ends with takeUntil(destroy$); ngOnDestroy calls next() then complete(). Fails when: takeUntil is not the last operator (see leaks), the subject is never nexted, or the pattern is copied into services that outlive components.

place.part: Part F — Resource and lifecycle doctrine

tools.title: takeUntilDestroyed and DestroyRef

transform.reason: Host destruction contexts and resource finalization are absent from the closed enum.

observable: Candidate traces show subscription cleanup at owner destruction.

tools.definition: Angular's operator completes a stream when the calling context (component, directive, service) is destroyed; call it inside an injection context or pass an injected DestroyRef when used in a method; stable since v19. Fails when: used in a long-lived service where 'destroyed' never happens, or called outside an injection context without a DestroyRef.

place.part: Part F — Resource and lifecycle doctrine

hooks.clause: BoardFacade and DotlnDialog use DestroyRef.onDestroy for imperative teardown; the operator is the stream twin

tools.title: Async pipe and interop as implicit unsubscribe

transform.reason: Template and interop owners need host lifecycle and read-model contracts.

observable: Candidate views associate each subscription with its consuming context.

tools.definition: AsyncPipe unsubscribes on destroy; toSignal cleans up with its owning context unless manualCleanup is set; rxLet/rxFor manage their own subscriptions; outputFromObservable stops forwarding on destroy. Template-edge subscription removes most manual lifecycle code.

tools.title: Subscription sink (add)

transform.reason: Parent-child subscription cleanup is resource ownership, not unit squad membership.

observable: Candidate traces show child subscriptions closing with their parent.

tools.definition: Problem: several imperative subscriptions in one owner. Shape: one parent Subscription; child subscriptions are add()-ed; unsubscribe once on destroy; remove() undoes an add. Fails when: a child is created after the parent was unsubscribed (it is closed immediately in modern RxJS, which can surprise), or when the sink hides streams that should have been composed.

tools.title: Values over time vs events over time

transform.reason: A current-value read model differs from event delivery and has no matching transform.

observable: Candidate views compare retained state with transient events.

tools.definition: The guide's own contrast: a stream of birthdays is a Subject, the resulting age is a BehaviorSubject (a current value). The same line divides signals (current values) from observables (events) in modern Angular.

tools.title: Finite streams need nothing
tools.definition: Streams that complete (HTTP, of, forkJoin, first()) release themselves; adding takeUntil to them is noise, and the eslint-angular prefer-takeuntil rule is configurable for that reason.

place.part: Part F — Resource and lifecycle doctrine

tools.title: connect/hold own the subscription

transform.reason: Owning subscriptions through state helpers requires a component lifetime model.

observable: Candidate traces show connected work released with its owner.

tools.definition: In RxAngular, connect and rxEffects' register own subscriptions and tear them down with the component, so components contain no subscribe calls (subscription-less components).

place.part: Part F — Resource and lifecycle doctrine

tools.title: takeUntil placed before a subscribing operator

transform.reason: Leaking inners depend on operator position and nested subscription propagation.

observable: Candidate traces reveal work continuing after an upstream stop.

tools.definition: If takeUntil precedes switchMap, combineLatest, shareReplay or similar, the notifier completes the outer but the inner or shared subscription keeps running. Rule: takeUntil last; lint no-unsafe-takeuntil (recommended).

tools.title: shareReplay without refCount

transform.reason: Fixing reference counts requires shared producer and subscription lifetime semantics.

observable: Candidate traces compare source activity after the last receiver leaves.

tools.definition: shareReplay(1) (refCount false) keeps the source subscribed after the last consumer leaves; long-lived sources (intervals, sockets, stores) then leak. Use shareReplay({bufferSize: 1, refCount: true}) or share with a ReplaySubject connector; lint no-sharereplay and no-sharereplay-before-takeuntil.

tools.title: Hot sources without completion
tools.definition: fromEvent, interval, subjects and sockets never complete on their own; every consumer must bound them (takeUntil, take, first, timeout) or own the teardown.

tools.title: Subjects completed by the wrong party

transform.reason: Completion authority belongs to a source owner and requires access and lifetime models.

observable: Candidate traces reveal one consumer ending service for other consumers.

tools.definition: Consumers must not call unsubscribe or complete on a shared subject (lint no-subject-unsubscribe): doing so ends it for every other consumer; only the owner completes it, in its own teardown.

tools.title: Ignored subscriptions and floating observables

transform.reason: Floating values and subscriptions require code dataflow and ownership checks.

observable: Candidate inspection locates unused producers and unowned live subscriptions.

tools.definition: Discarding the Subscription returned by subscribe (no-ignored-subscription) or dropping an observable returned by a function without subscribing or returning it (no-ignored-observable, no-floating-observables) hides either a leak or a no-op.

tools.title: toSignal called repeatedly

transform.reason: Repeated signal conversion creates resource instances requiring host lifecycle semantics.

observable: Candidate traces compare conversion calls with the number of live subscriptions.

tools.definition: Each toSignal call opens a subscription; calling it in a getter, template or loop multiplies subscriptions. Create it once and reuse the signal.

tools.title: ReplaySubject without a buffer size

transform.reason: Finite retained history cannot represent the unbounded replay-buffer anti-pattern.

observable: Candidate trace: retained message history grows with every delivery without a history cap.
Candidate trace: a late receiver is offered the entire accumulated message history.

analog.clause: Diagnose retained agent context or work history growing without a bound.

tools.definition: An unbounded ReplaySubject (or publishReplay/shareReplay without a size) remembers everything forever; always set the buffer (lint no-ignored-replay-buffer).

tools.title: Finalization is guaranteed
tools.definition: Producer cleanup runs on error, complete or unsubscribe; a custom observable returns its teardown from the subscribe function; operators pass finalization through. Trust it rather than adding manual cleanup paths.

tools.title: Time as a dimension: the burst-compression family

transform.reason: The timing family contains incompatible survivor and window rules; one must be selected.

observable: Candidate timelines compare first, latest and grouped deliveries.

tools.definition: debounce, throttle, audit, sample and bufferTime are one idea (compress a burst) with different answers to which value survives and when: debounce waits for silence then emits the last; throttle emits the first per window (optionally the trailing); audit emits the last at window end; sample emits the latest on a tick; bufferTime keeps all as an array.

tools.title: Teardown ordering
tools.definition: On unsubscribe, downstream operators tear down first and the source last (each operator function unsubscribes the observable it wrapped); finalize callbacks therefore run after the inner teardowns of later operators and before upstream ones. Inference from the operator-function model; verify with a marble test before relying on exact order.

tools.title: Completion as a signal

transform.reason: Completion propagation and finalization are resource-lifecycle operations outside the enum.

observable: Candidate traces distinguish observable termination from silent cancellation.

tools.definition: Prefer designs where streams complete (take, first, takeUntil) because completion propagates to consumers and triggers finalization; unsubscribe is silent to downstream code.

place.part: Part F — Resource and lifecycle doctrine

tools.title: Closed subjects
tools.definition: A completed or errored subject stays closed; later next() calls are dropped (lint no-redundant-notify). Components re-created after destroy need new subjects, so declare them per instance, never statically.

tools.title: Resource with abortSignal

transform.reason: Aborting loaders requires an external resource, cancellation signal and parameter contract.

observable: Candidate traces show replacement parameters aborting a prior load.

tools.definition: Angular's resource aborts an in-flight loader when params change and hands the loader an AbortSignal for fetch; the signal-world analogue of switchMap cancellation.

hooks.clause: a status-route loader keyed by store or order id gets cancellation for free

tools.title: TestScheduler.run with virtual time

transform.reason: Virtual-clock execution and test assertions are not any closed scene transform.

observable: Candidate timelines compare actual events with expected virtual-time events.

tools.definition: Inside run(callback), operators that use the async scheduler (delay, debounceTime, timeouts) automatically use virtual time, so time-based code is tested synchronously and deterministically; assertions scheduled by helpers execute when the callback returns or on flush().

tools.title: Helpers: cold, hot, expectObservable, expectSubscriptions, time, animate

transform.reason: Test helpers need fixtures and assertions rather than a scene effect.

observable: Candidate timelines show source lifetimes beside expected emissions.

tools.definition: cold creates an observable that starts on subscription; hot behaves as already running (with ^ as the subscription point); expectObservable(actual, subscriptionMarbles).toBe(marbles, values, error) asserts emissions; expectSubscriptions asserts when sources were subscribed/unsubscribed; time converts marbles to frames; animate declares when requestAnimationFrame callbacks fire.

tools.title: Marble syntax
tools.definition: '-' one frame; alphanumerics emit values (mapped via a values object); '|' complete; '#' error; '()' groups events in one frame; '^' subscription point for hot sources; whitespace ignored for alignment; time progression as a number plus ms/s/m, which must be space-padded when not first; a value marble itself advances one frame, so expected timings often subtract 1 ms.

tools.title: Subscription marbles
tools.definition: A separate diagram with at most one '^' (subscribe) and one '!' (unsubscribe) plus '-' and time progression; passed to expectObservable to bound a never-completing stream or to expectSubscriptions to assert source lifetimes.

tools.title: Testing hot vs cold

transform.reason: Hot and cold test sources need an execution model and expected subscription histories.

observable: Candidate timelines compare receiver start times with source activations.

tools.definition: Use hot when the source emits regardless of subscribers (shared stores, sockets) and assert multiple subscribers with different ^ points; use cold for per-subscriber producers (HTTP) and assert with expectSubscriptions that the operator subscribed and unsubscribed when expected (e.g. switchMap cancelling).

tools.title: Synchronous assertion after flush

transform.reason: Driving a test clock and checking side effects requires an expected-effect contract.

observable: Candidate views compare the effect state after all scheduled work runs.

tools.definition: To check side effects (a tap updating a variable), call flush() inside run to drive virtual time to completion, then assert.

tools.title: Operator decision tree

transform.reason: An operator chooser lacks a scene-specific decision procedure and executable outcome.

observable: Candidate inspection records a stream requirement and the selected operator.

tools.definition: The official interactive chooser walks from 'I have one existing observable, and…' to an operator name; teams use its phrasing as a shared vocabulary in review.

tools.title: Promises are not virtualised
tools.definition: Code that consumes promises or other non-RxJS scheduling cannot be reliably marble-tested; isolate it and test it with the framework's async tools. delay(0) likewise cannot be asserted at frame zero.

tools.title: Behaviour outside run()
tools.definition: Legacy use of TestScheduler without run has different semantics: verbose helper names, no auto scheduler substitution, no time-progression syntax, 10 ms frames, a 750-frame cap and explicit flush; it is discouraged.

tools.title: Marble tests cost

transform.reason: Choosing timing assertions versus value assertions is a validation decision.

observable: Candidate views compare assertion detail with the behavior being checked.

tools.definition: Marble tests pin exact timing and require understanding hot/cold, schedulers and the syntax; they are the right tool for operators and time-based composition and the wrong tool for 'did the facade emit these values in order'.

tools.title: observer-spy approach

transform.reason: Observation and assertions need a test harness and expectations, not a scene transition.

observable: Candidate views record received values, completion and errors for inspection.

tools.definition: subscribeSpyTo(observable) records values, completion and error; assert with getValues, getFirstValue, getLastValue, getValueAt, getValuesLength, receivedNext/receivedComplete/receivedError, getError; await onComplete/onError; expectErrors: true opts into capturing errors; autoUnsubscribe/queueForAutoUnsubscribe clean up; fakeTime (or Angular fakeAsync) controls timers.

tools.title: Values and order over frames

transform.reason: Assertion scope is a test-design choice without an executable scene operation.

observable: Candidate inspection distinguishes sequence failures from frame mismatches.

tools.definition: Most unit tests only need the received values and their order; reserve frame-exact assertions for operators and timing contracts.

tools.title: fakeAsync and tick for time

transform.reason: Framework timer virtualization requires a host test clock and timer execution model.

observable: Candidate timelines show timer advancement and resulting events.

tools.definition: In Angular tests, fakeAsync with tick/flush drives timers used by debounceTime or timer without the TestScheduler; mixing both in one test is a known source of confusion.

tools.title: Zoneless TestBed

transform.reason: Component stabilization and notification validation need a host rendering test environment.

observable: Candidate views show when a component becomes stable and visible.

tools.definition: TestBed is zoneless by default in current Angular: prefer await fixture.whenStable() over detectChanges(); provideCheckNoChangesConfig({exhaustive: true, interval}) can catch bindings that changed without notifying.

tools.title: Test facades, mappers and wrappers

transform.reason: Test boundary selection needs fixtures and behavioral expectations for each component.

observable: Candidate inspection associates behavior with facade, mapper and presentation tests.

tools.definition: Behavioural tests concentrate on the facade (stream/vm logic), pure mappers and platform wrappers; presentation gets DOM assertions and real-browser tests for focus and keyboard behaviour.

tools.title: Testing container components

transform.reason: Container wiring tests need input fixtures and expected derived outputs.

observable: Candidate traces connect controlled input streams to presentation values.

tools.definition: Nielsen's approach: isolate the container's stream wiring from presentation, drive inputs through observables and assert the derived outputs; a container test is a stream test.

tools.title: Testing effects and stores

transform.reason: Store and effect testing requires state fixtures, actions and expected results.

observable: Candidate traces compare dispatched inputs with selected state and emitted actions.

tools.definition: NgRx effects are tested by feeding an actions stream (mock actions provider) and asserting emitted actions with marbles or spies; stores by dispatching and selecting; component stores by calling updaters/effects and reading selectors.

tools.definition: Operators pick the scheduler introducing the least concurrency that still satisfies their contract; synchronous delivery is the default, and schedulers are opt-in tools, not a mental model to start from.

transform.reason: Testing alternatives does not select a runtime strategy or define the inner work.

observable: Candidate timelines compare replacement, rejection, sequencing and overlap.

tools.definition: A test per flattening choice: switchMap unsubscribes the first inner on a second outer value (expectSubscriptions), exhaustMap ignores the second, concatMap delays it, mergeMap overlaps; these are the regression tests for the read/write rule.

tools.title: Test teardown explicitly

transform.reason: Teardown assertions require resource identities and expected subscription lifetimes.

observable: Candidate traces compare cancellation time with resource release.

tools.definition: Assert that unsubscribing (subscription marbles '!') ends the source subscription and that finalize ran; leaks are regressions you can test with expectSubscriptions.

tools.title: Scheduler = data structure + execution context + virtual clock
tools.definition: A scheduler queues tasks, decides where/when they run (sync, microtask, macrotask, animation frame) and owns a now() clock; it controls when a subscription starts and when notifications are delivered.

tools.title: Scheduler types
tools.definition: null (sync, recursive; constant-time work), queueScheduler (trampoline in the current frame; iteration), asapScheduler (microtask, like promises; async conversions), asyncScheduler (setInterval; time-based work), animationFrameScheduler (before the next repaint; animation).

tools.title: observeOn vs subscribeOn

transform.reason: Source-start scheduling and notification scheduling need execution-context semantics.

observable: Candidate timelines distinguish producer start from receiver delivery.

tools.definition: observeOn(scheduler) re-schedules the delivery of notifications downstream of its position; subscribeOn(scheduler) schedules the subscribe call itself (when the producer starts); creation and time operators accept a scheduler argument for the same purpose.

tools.title: observeOn(animationFrameScheduler) for rendering

transform.reason: Frame scheduling and latest-value coalescing are distinct alternatives needing a chosen contract.

observable: Candidate timelines compare scheduled deliveries with frame-end aggregation.

tools.definition: Problem: high-frequency updates repaint too often. Shape: values$.pipe(observeOn(animationFrameScheduler)) or auditTime(0, animationFrameScheduler) coalesces deliveries to once per frame. Fails when: delays are involved (falls back to async) or when the consumer is not a render.

tools.title: Scheduler injection for tests

transform.reason: Injecting a virtual scheduler changes test execution infrastructure outside the enum.

observable: Candidate traces compare a fixed pipeline under real and virtual clocks.

tools.definition: Operators take a scheduler so production code can be driven by virtual time under TestScheduler.run without changing the pipeline; inside run() the substitution is automatic for async-scheduler operators.

tools.title: zone.js auto-detection vs explicit notification
tools.definition: With zone.js, any async task may trigger change detection for the whole tree; zoneless Angular refreshes views only on explicit notifications: a signal read in the template changed, markForCheck (which AsyncPipe calls), setInput, template/host event listeners, or a dirty view reattached.

tools.title: Zoneless by default (v21)
tools.definition: Zoneless is the default from Angular v21 (opt-in via provideZonelessChangeDetection in v20); remove zone.js from polyfills; NgZone stability observables never emit; use afterNextRender/afterEveryRender or MutationObserver instead of onStable; PendingTasks keeps SSR waiting for async work.

hooks.clause: DotLn-Angular's core composes zoneless change detection already

tools.title: OnPush + async pipe

transform.reason: Component invalidation and rendering require a host UI lifecycle.

observable: Candidate views show redraws caused by incoming values.

tools.definition: OnPush components re-render only on input changes, template events or markForCheck; AsyncPipe marks for check on each emission, so stream-driven OnPush components render exactly when data changes. Fails when: state is mutated in a subscribe callback without a notification (zoneless shows nothing).

tools.title: Declarative vs imperative RxJS

transform.reason: Composing a dependency graph instead of assignments is a program-structure change.

observable: Candidate views show derived outputs without a separate assignment path.

tools.definition: Using observables does not make code declarative: subscribing and assigning is imperative. Declarative means composing streams so the result derives itself; the recurring question is whether a subscribe is needed at all.

tools.title: Signals as the scheduling primitive
tools.definition: A signal read in a template schedules a refresh of exactly the views that read it; toObservable batches rapid signal updates into one emission after the signal stabilises; RxAngular strategies offer the same locality for streams.

tools.title: Forms in zoneless apps

transform.reason: Form-to-view notification requires host component and form state models.

observable: Candidate views reveal a state change that did or did not schedule a redraw.

tools.definition: Reactive form updates do not schedule rendering; connect valueChanges to a signal or call markForCheck when the template depends on structural changes.

tools.title: distinctUntilChanged at derivation boundaries

observable: A message equal to the preceding accepted payload is suppressed.
A changed payload is delivered and becomes the next comparison value.

tools.definition: Cut repeated emissions of equal state before expensive derivations or renders; with a key selector it compares a chosen property; selectors and signal equality play the same role.

tools.title: Share expensive sources

transform.reason: Sharing expensive work requires producer identity and subscriber lifetime semantics.

observable: Candidate traces compare consumers with actual producer executions.

tools.definition: share/shareReplay(refCount) make one producer serve many consumers; the alternative is N requests or N folds for N template bindings.

tools.title: auditTime/throttleTime for UI cadence

transform.reason: Audit and throttle choose different surviving values; the cadence alone does not select a policy.

observable: Candidate timelines compare first-value and latest-value bounded delivery.

tools.definition: Bound UI update frequency to what a human can perceive (frame rate or ~100 ms) with auditTime or throttleTime rather than rendering every event.

tools.title: Debounce heavy derived work

transform.reason: Avoiding derived-state glitches requires a dependency graph and a stabilization boundary.

observable: Candidate traces reveal intermediate combinations before inputs settle.

tools.definition: When several inputs change together, debounceTime(0) or auditTime(0) on the combined stream avoids glitch renders of intermediate combinations.

tools.title: Local render strategies (RxAngular)

transform.reason: Rendering a component subtree is a host operation, not zooming the level of description.

observable: Candidate views show which components redraw for one state change.

tools.definition: rxLet/rxFor/push with a strategy such as 'local' render only the affected component instead of marking ancestors; the stream-world equivalent of signal-granular updates.

tools.title: Measure before scheduling

transform.reason: Profiling needs a workload and measurement harness rather than a scene transform.

observable: Candidate views compare time spent rendering, subscribing and scheduling.

tools.definition: Hladky's performance teaching: profile (DevTools, flame charts) before adding schedulers or strategies; most wins come from fewer change-detection cycles and fewer subscriptions, not from exotic schedulers.

tools.title: Nested subscribes

transform.reason: Replacing nested subscriptions needs an explicit flattening and ownership contract.

observable: Candidate traces show inner work escaping its parent lifetime.

tools.definition: subscribe inside a subscribe callback: inner subscriptions escape cancellation, order is undefined, errors are not propagated; replace with a flattening operator. Lint no-nested-subscribe (recommended).

tools.title: Subscribe in services

transform.reason: Service subscription boundaries are code ownership and lifetime decisions.

observable: Candidate views locate hidden state and unowned service subscriptions.

tools.definition: A service that subscribes and stores results in fields becomes a hidden cache with no lifetime and no error path; services should return streams and let consumers compose. Lint prefer-composition (optionally scoped to services).

tools.title: Reactive = derived values stay current

transform.reason: Maintaining derived values needs dependency and projection functions outside the enum.

observable: Candidate views show derived state following source revisions.

tools.definition: A value derived from other values updates when its sources change without an explicit step; data streams (from services) and action streams (from the UI) are the two kinds of source.

tools.title: Subscribe-and-assign in components

transform.reason: Replacing copied component fields needs a host read model and subscription owner.

observable: Candidate views compare assigned fields with stream-derived presentation.

tools.definition: Subscribing in ngOnInit to copy values into fields re-creates imperative state and needs manual unsubscribe; bind the stream in the template or convert with toSignal. Lint prefer-async-pipe.

tools.title: Imperative mutation inside tap

transform.reason: Replacing imperative mutations requires a state schema and pure derivation function.

observable: Candidate traces identify state writes hidden in observation callbacks.

tools.definition: Using tap to write component fields or external state turns the pipeline into a side-effect chain whose order and timing are opaque, and under zoneless Angular the mutation may never render; derive state with scan/map or write through a store.

hooks.clause: zoneless core makes this failure visible: a tap-mutated field does not re-render

tools.title: Subscribe inside operators

transform.reason: Callback-created subscriptions require a resource graph and ownership checks.

observable: Candidate views reveal subscriptions created outside their parent's lifetime.

tools.definition: subscribe calls within map/tap/switchMap callbacks create orphan subscriptions. Lint no-subscribe-in-pipe.

tools.title: Ignoring errors at subscribe

transform.reason: Failure handling needs a handler and exception-reporting model.

observable: Candidate traces expose failures with no observing consumer.

tools.definition: subscribe(next) with no error handler and no upstream catchError lets failures escape as unhandled errors. Lint no-ignored-error.

tools.title: toPromise
tools.definition: toPromise resolves undefined on an empty completion and hides the multi-value nature; use firstValueFrom/lastValueFrom with a default value. Lint no-topromise; deprecation page to-promise.

tools.title: Subjects as public API

transform.reason: Read-only exposure and authorized emission are API access-control properties.

observable: Candidate views distinguish consumer read access from producer write access.

tools.definition: Exposing a Subject lets any consumer emit, error or complete the stream for everyone; expose asObservable or a signal and provide intent methods. Lint no-exposed-subjects.

tools.title: Reading BehaviorSubject.value

transform.reason: Imperative state reads versus reactive context needs a state and dependency model.

observable: Candidate traces reveal decisions made from stale snapshots.

tools.definition: Pulling the current value imperatively bypasses the stream and races with updates; derive with withLatestFrom or keep it in a signal. Lint no-subject-value.

tools.title: Over-sharing

transform.reason: Sharing cost and correctness depend on producer identity and lifetime, which are unspecified.

observable: Candidate traces compare shared producers with unnecessary retained work.

tools.definition: Putting share/shareReplay on every stream hides the cold/hot decision, keeps producers alive longer than needed and can replay errors; share only where multiple consumers of one producer are intended.

tools.title: shareReplay as a cache without invalidation

transform.reason: Cache invalidation requires refresh triggers, source execution and stored result state.

observable: Candidate traces compare cached results with later invalidation and refresh.

tools.definition: shareReplay(1) on a data stream turns into a cache that never refreshes; pair it with a trigger stream (switchMap over refresh$) or a time window.

tools.title: Subject where a creation function would do

transform.reason: Choosing an event adapter requires an external API and listener lifecycle.

observable: Candidate views compare manual bridges with directly owned event adapters.

tools.definition: Hand-wiring a Subject to bridge a callback API when fromEvent, fromEventPattern, defer or bindCallback express it directly; subjects are for multicasting and imperative bridges that have no creation function.

tools.title: Push versus pull

transform.reason: Producer-driven versus consumer-driven timing needs a demand protocol absent from the enum.

observable: Candidate traces compare who initiates each transfer.

tools.definition: Pull: the consumer decides when to take a value (functions, iterators); push: the producer decides when to deliver (promises, observables). The first design question for any feature is who should control timing.

tools.title: Conveyor-belt model
tools.definition: Morony's picture: streams are belts, operators are machines on the belt, subscribing is taking an item off; the template is where items leave the belt.

tools.title: Unsubscribing a subject

transform.reason: Shared-source closure and owner authority require a subscription lifecycle model.

observable: Candidate traces show effects of one consumer closing a shared source.

tools.definition: Calling unsubscribe on a Subject tears it down for all observers and makes later use throw; complete it from its owner instead. Lint no-subject-unsubscribe.

tools.title: Forgetting completion semantics

transform.reason: Multiple completion and aggregation rules are listed without one executable source contract.

observable: Candidate timelines reveal waits caused by empty or unfinished sources.

tools.definition: forkJoin over a never-completing source never emits; combineLatest waits for every input; first() on an empty stream errors; a never-completing inner stalls concatMap. Always know whether each source completes.

tools.title: Assuming asynchrony

transform.reason: Synchronous producer execution requires evaluation-order semantics outside the enum.

observable: Candidate traces compare state observed before and after subscription returns.

tools.definition: Observables may emit synchronously on subscribe (of, BehaviorSubject, cached shareReplay), so code that assumes a later tick (reading a field after subscribe) breaks; design for both.

tools.title: switchMap on writes

transform.reason: Preserving writes requires choosing queue, overlap or rejection plus write-completion semantics.

observable: Candidate traces reveal superseding intents interrupting earlier writes.

tools.definition: Cancelling an in-flight write when the user acts again loses data; use concatMap, mergeMap or exhaustMap. Lint no-unsafe-switchmap for effects.

tools.title: takeUntil before the operator it should stop

transform.reason: Stopping downstream work requires operator-order and nested subscription semantics.

observable: Candidate traces show whether a stop signal reaches every active inner.

tools.definition: Operators after takeUntil keep their own subscriptions alive; put takeUntil last. Lint no-unsafe-takeuntil.

tools.title: first/take inside effects

transform.reason: Outer effect completion versus inner completion requires scoped subscription lifetimes.

observable: Candidate traces reveal an effect no longer reacting after its first input.

tools.definition: An effect that completes after one action stops reacting forever; take-style operators belong inside the inner stream. Lint no-unsafe-first.

tools.title: Cyclic actions

transform.reason: Detecting self-triggering actions requires an effect dependency graph and action schema.

observable: Candidate traces show the same action repeatedly causing its own emission.

tools.definition: An effect that re-emits an action matching its own ofType filter loops forever. Lint no-cyclic-action.

tools.title: startWith under resubscription

transform.reason: Repeated initialization depends on resubscription and effect lifecycle semantics.

observable: Candidate traces show startup work repeated after an outer failure.

tools.definition: Because NgRx resubscribes an errored effect, a startWith in the effect pipe fires again on each resubscription, repeating its side effect; handle errors inside so the main stream never errors.

tools.title: Ignoring the notifier in retryWhen/repeatWhen

transform.reason: Notifier causality needs source and notifier execution semantics.

observable: Candidate traces show retries occurring without a corresponding failure signal.

tools.definition: A notifier function that returns a stream not derived from its input retries unconditionally and immediately. Lint no-ignored-notifier.

tools.title: RxJS for everything

transform.reason: Primitive selection is a design choice without a concrete event or state contract.

observable: Candidate inspection compares timing requirements with subscription overhead.

tools.definition: Wrapping synchronous state, constants and simple derivations in streams adds subscriptions and timing questions for no benefit; keep synchronous state in signals or plain values and use streams for events over time.

hooks.clause: DotLn-Angular's board feature is signals-only today; add streams only for events over time

tools.title: Reactive thinking is a habit change
tools.definition: Pearson's framing: reactive code resists mastery not because the API is hard but because it requires thinking in whole streams first; it clicks after sustained practice, and resistance is better treated as a habit to change than a skill gap.

hooks.clause: worker prompts that ask for the stream shape first reduce imperative drift

tools.title: Storing derived state

transform.reason: Removing stored derivations needs state ownership and projection functions.

observable: Candidate views compare canonical state with duplicate derived copies.

tools.definition: Writing a derivation into state (and then keeping it in sync) instead of selecting it; RxAngular's and SignalStore's guidance is to derive with select/computed.

tools.title: Lifecycle authority in the view

transform.reason: Lifecycle legality and UI intent authority need a state-machine ownership contract.

observable: Candidate views reveal multiple authorities deciding the same transition.

tools.definition: Deriving legality or state transitions inside the UI from a projection duplicates the machine and drifts; the UI renders evidence and sends intents.

hooks.clause: component rule H5

tools.title: God stream

transform.reason: Splitting a pipeline by concern is a code graph refactor without a runtime transform.

observable: Candidate views separate inputs, loading, cache, errors and persistence stages.

tools.definition: One pipeline that handles input, fetching, caching, error UI and persistence; split into named streams per concern and compose them.

verified.note: RX-OPS (extract sequences with pipe); framing MK

tools.title: Effects that write state directly

transform.reason: A unique write path requires state ownership, event schemas and update contracts.

observable: Candidate traces show a single change reaching state through multiple paths.

tools.definition: An effect patching state and also dispatching creates two write paths; effects should emit actions (or use tapResponse to patch) but not both for the same change.

tools.title: eslint-plugin-rxjs rule families
tools.definition: Jamieson's plugin codifies the doctrine: subscription hygiene (no-nested-subscribe, no-ignored-subscription, no-ignored-error, no-async-subscribe), subject hygiene (no-exposed-subjects, no-subject-unsubscribe, no-subject-value, suffix-subjects), sharing (no-sharereplay, no-ignored-replay-buffer, no-connectable), effects/epics safety (no-cyclic-action, no-unsafe-catch, no-unsafe-first, no-unsafe-switchmap, no-unsafe-takeuntil), API hygiene (no-create, no-index, no-internal, no-compat, no-topromise, no-unbound-methods, prefer-observer, throw-error, no-implicit-any-catch), style (finnish/no-finnish, just, ban-operators, ban-observables).

tools.title: eslint-plugin-rxjs-x additions
tools.definition: The maintained successor adds no-floating-observables, no-misused-observables, no-ignored-default-value, no-sharereplay-before-takeuntil, no-subscribe-in-pipe, no-unnecessary-collection and prefer-root-operators (import from rxjs, not rxjs/operators).

tools.title: eslint-plugin-rxjs-angular
tools.definition: Three Angular rules: prefer-async-pipe (no subscribe in components), prefer-composition (subscriptions must be composed, optionally in services/directives/pipes), prefer-takeuntil (subscribe needs an accompanying takeUntil, configurable).

tools.title: prefer-observer
tools.definition: Pass an observer object to subscribe and tap rather than positional handlers; the deprecations page subscribe-arguments records the same direction.

tools.title: Signals for values, observables for events

transform.reason: Value versus event primitives require a state and timing contract before choosing behavior.

observable: Candidate views compare synchronous reads with temporally composed events.

tools.definition: Signals hold synchronous state and derive from it (signal, computed, linkedSignal); observables model events over time (user input, transport, timers) where cancellation, ordering and retry matter. The two are complementary, bridged by interop functions.

tools.title: Pull-based signals, push-based streams

transform.reason: Pull reads, dependency tracking and pushed events require distinct evaluation models.

observable: Candidate views show when computation occurs relative to reads and updates.

tools.definition: A signal is read (pulled) and recomputes lazily when dependencies change; an observable pushes. Signals are glitch-resistant by construction for synchronous graphs; streams need debounce or restructuring to avoid intermediate states.

tools.title: Compose events and async actions as one model

transform.reason: Unifying event sources is an architectural abstraction, without a concrete toy transition.

observable: Candidate views connect input, timer and transport sources to one composition.

tools.definition: Hladky's and Wortmann's teaching line: UI events, timers, transport and state are all streams, so one composition model covers heavily dynamic UIs; local component state deserves the same reactive treatment as global state.

tools.title: effect is for the outside world

transform.reason: Effect placement versus pure derivation is code structure and state ownership.

observable: Candidate views distinguish external synchronization from computed state.

tools.definition: effect and afterRenderEffect synchronise signals with non-reactive APIs (DOM, logging, storage); they are not for deriving state, which is computed's job. The stream-world twin is tap at the edge versus scan/map for derivation.

tools.title: toSignal

transform.reason: Signal retention, reads, errors and owner cleanup require a host signal lifecycle.

observable: Candidate traces show a retained value and the fate of its source subscription.

tools.definition: Observable → signal: subscribes immediately; initialValue or undefined before the first emission; requireSync for synchronously emitting sources (BehaviorSubject, shareReplay with a value); custom equal; cleanup with the owning context or manualCleanup; an error from the observable is thrown when the signal is read; after completion the signal keeps the last value.

tools.title: toObservable

transform.reason: Signal stabilization and effect-owned subscription require a reactive dependency model.

observable: Candidate traces show multiple state changes producing one stabilized event.

tools.definition: Signal → observable: tracks the signal through an effect, buffers via a ReplaySubject, may emit the current value synchronously on subscribe, emits later values asynchronously and only after the signal settles (rapid updates collapse to the last); needs an injection context or an Injector.

tools.title: takeUntilDestroyed

transform.reason: Destruction contexts and subscription cleanup need a host ownership lifecycle.

observable: Candidate traces show source cleanup when its owner ends.

tools.definition: Completes a stream when the component/directive/service is destroyed; injection context or explicit DestroyRef; stable since v19.

tools.title: outputFromObservable / outputToObservable

transform.reason: Component output adapters require a host output API and destruction lifecycle.

tools.definition: An observable becomes a component output (forwarding stops on destroy; only callable in property initializers; prefer output() when emitting imperatively); an output becomes an observable for operator use.

tools.title: Store-level bridges

transform.reason: Store bridges need state schemas, signal reads and concrete update pipelines.

tools.definition: SignalStore's rxMethod runs an RxJS pipeline against signal or observable inputs and patches state; withProps exposes toObservable streams; RxAngular's rxState offers select (observable) and signal/computed (signal) views over one state.

tools.title: resource(params, loader)

transform.reason: Resource states, loaders and cancellation require an async resource state machine.

observable: Candidate traces show parameter changes, reloads and result states.

tools.definition: Async data as signals: params is a reactive computation; the loader runs when params change (not when undefined) and receives an abortSignal; status is idle, loading, reloading, resolved, error or local; value, hasValue, error, isLoading and snapshot are signals; reload() reruns; chain links resources; set/update create local values.

tools.title: rxResource

tools.title: Streams of intent (composite architecture)

transform.reason: The intent-state-view loop requires reducers and effects; it is not a loop across levels.

observable: Candidate views trace an intent through state, presentation and new events.

tools.definition: Problem: UI code that mutates fields from many callbacks. Shape: every user or system event becomes a value on an intent/action stream; state is a fold (scan or reducer) over that stream; views derive from state (combineLatest/selectors); side effects consume actions at the edge and feed new actions back. Fails when: effects mutate state directly, when the action stream is public, or when derived views are stored instead of computed. The composite label is the brief's; its parts are sourced individually.

observable: Candidate traces connect method input to resulting state changes.

tools.definition: SignalStore's bridge from RxJS to signals: a method defined as an operator pipeline (debounceTime, distinctUntilChanged, switchMap, tapResponse) that accepts a value, a signal or an observable, patching state as results arrive.

transform.reason: Mapping event types into partial state requires case reducers and a state schema.

observable: Candidate traces show event-driven updates and derived reads.

observable: Candidate views distinguish stored fields from derived values and effects.

tools.definition: Functional local state: set initial state; connect streams into keys or reduce them; select(key or keys, projector) as observables; signal(key), computed and computedFrom for signal reads; rxEffects registers side-effect subscriptions; nothing is stored that can be derived.

tools.title: RxAngular template and render strategies

transform.reason: Component rendering and browser scheduling are outside the closed scene transforms.

observable: Candidate views count redraws within the affected component.

tools.title: Facade with a subject behind it

transform.reason: Facade encapsulation and lifecycle authority are API ownership properties.

tools.definition: Problem: components should not know store internals. Shape: an injectable holds private subjects or state and exposes read-only selections (asObservable or signals) plus intent methods. Fails when: subjects leak through public fields, when the facade subscribes internally and re-exposes values via mutable fields, or when the facade grows lifecycle authority it should not have.

transform.reason: Immediate subscription, signal reads and context cleanup need a host read model.

tools.title: Typeahead

transform.reason: Query equality, cancellable searches and result ordering need a search contract beyond delivery timing.

observable: Candidate traces compare query changes with displayed search results.

tools.definition: Problem: search while typing without flooding the server or showing stale results. Shape: input$.pipe(debounceTime(n), distinctUntilChanged(), switchMap(q => search(q))). Fails when: the inner request errors without a catchError (the whole typeahead dies), mergeMap replaces switchMap (out-of-order results), or short/empty queries are not filtered.

tools.title: Submit button: exhaustMap

observable: While one delivery awaits acknowledgement, new incoming messages are discarded.
A later message is accepted after the active delivery finishes.

tools.definition: Problem: double clicks start duplicate writes. Shape: submit$.pipe(exhaustMap(() => save())) ignores triggers while one write is in flight. Fails when: the second intent should queue (concatMap) rather than be dropped, or when the inner never completes and the button stays dead.

hooks.clause: a repeated dispatch phrase while an order runs is an exhaustMap case

verified.note: RX-SRC exhaustMap; JAM-SWITCHMAP; NGRX-FX (exhaustMap in examples); LRX (swipe-to-refresh)

tools.title: Flattening choice: reads vs writes

transform.reason: The read-write distinction does not select one concurrency policy without operation semantics.

observable: Candidate traces compare replacement, overlap, queuing and rejection.

tools.definition: Reads that supersede earlier ones: switchMap. Independent writes that may overlap: mergeMap. Writes that must keep order: concatMap. Ignore repeats while busy: exhaustMap. The named bug class is switchMap cancelling an in-flight write (add-to-cart); lint no-unsafe-switchmap flags it in effects.

hooks.clause: appends to the control log are ordered writes (concatMap); status reads are switchMap

tools.title: Operator vs operator function
tools.definition: An operator (map, mergeMap) is a factory that returns an operator function; an operator function maps an observable to a new observable and nothing else; pipe composes operator functions left to right.

tools.title: Ordered writes: concatMap

observable: Messages wait in arrival order while one delivery awaits acknowledgement.
The next queued delivery starts only when the active delivery finishes.

tools.definition: Problem: writes must land in order. Shape: writes$.pipe(concatMap(w => persist(w))) runs one inner at a time, queueing the rest. Fails when: one inner never completes (queue stalls forever: add timeout), or the queue grows without bound under a fast producer.

hooks.clause: the skeleton's serialized store writer is this shape

tools.title: Form value streams

transform.reason: Form event schemas, parent-child ordering and render notifications require a form model.

observable: Candidate traces relate field edits to parent state and validation events.

tools.definition: Problem: react to form edits. Shape: control.valueChanges (and statusChanges) piped with debounceTime/distinctUntilChanged; the newer unified events stream carries typed value/status/pristine/touched events and replaces combineLatest over the two. Fails when: a child's valueChanges is read before the parent updated (subscribe to the parent's events), when emitEvent:false silences expected emissions, or in zoneless apps where structural form changes need markForCheck or signals.

tools.title: Gestures as streams (drag and drop)

transform.reason: Pointer phases, coordinates and listener lifetimes need a gesture model.

observable: Candidate traces show a drag starting, moving and stopping.

tools.definition: Problem: pointer sequences spanning down, move and up. Shape: down$.pipe(switchMap(start => move$.pipe(map(delta), takeUntil(up$)))) yields one inner drag per press. Fails when: move/up listeners attach to the element rather than the document (moves lost outside it), when takeUntil sits before map (fine) but before the switchMap (inner keeps running), or when passive listeners block preventDefault.

hooks.clause: the roadmap's drag-equip surface for console v1 is this shape

verified.note: LRX (lockscreen, swipe-to-refresh); canonical drag form MK; DOTLN

tools.title: Swipe to refresh

transform.reason: Gesture thresholds, refresh execution and rearming need a gesture-resource state machine.

observable: Candidate traces show pulls that cross a threshold and start one refresh.

tools.definition: Touch-start starts a tracked pull (switchMap/takeUntil), a threshold decides via iif whether to refresh, exhaustMap guards the refresh, finalize resets, repeat re-arms.

tools.title: Parallel fetch: forkJoin

transform.reason: Last-value aggregation needs payload schemas and multi-source completion semantics.

observable: Candidate timelines show one combined result after all sources finish.

tools.definition: Problem: wait for several finite requests. Shape: forkJoin({a: a$, b: b$}) emits once with each source's last value when all complete, then completes. Fails when: any source never completes (never emits), any completes without a value (completes empty), or any errors (the join errors and unsubscribes the rest). Use for one-shot requests only.

tools.title: Parallel live streams: combineLatest

transform.reason: A latest-value join needs multiple retained payloads and a projection function.

observable: Candidate timelines show outputs only after every input has a value.

tools.definition: For sources that keep emitting: emits on every change once all inputs have emitted; completes when all complete; errors if any errors; an input that completes keeps its last value in the combination.

tools.title: Request deduplication

transform.reason: Deduplication requires shared producer identity and reset semantics beyond channel delivery.

observable: Candidate traces compare receiver count with actual source executions.

tools.definition: Problem: N subscribers trigger N identical requests. Shape: request$.pipe(share()) joins concurrent subscribers to one in-flight request; shareReplay({bufferSize: 1, refCount: true}) also serves late subscribers from the cached result. Fails when: a late subscriber after completion re-triggers (share resets on complete by default), when an errored shared stream stays errored (resetOnError), or when refCount is false and the source lives forever.

hooks.clause: one shared projection per tick instead of every viewer re-reading the whole event log

tools.title: Optimistic update with rollback

transform.reason: Rollback needs state snapshots, entity versions and compensating update rules.

observable: Candidate traces show provisional changes, confirmations and compensations.

tools.definition: Problem: show a change before the server confirms. Shape: emit the optimistic state change immediately, run the write with concatMap or exhaustMap, capture the prior snapshot with withLatestFrom, and on error emit a compensating action that restores it. Fails when: concurrent optimistic edits interleave (track per-entity versions), the rollback restores a snapshot older than later confirmed writes, or the UI never shows the failure.

tools.title: Cancellation: switchMap and takeUntil

transform.reason: Cancelling arbitrary inner work requires a cancellable resource and subscription graph.

observable: Candidate traces show whether superseded or stopped work releases its resources.

tools.definition: Problem: stop work that no longer matters. Shape: switchMap cancels the previous inner when a new outer value arrives; takeUntil(stop$) completes a stream when a notifier emits. Fails when: the inner is not cancellable (fetch needs an AbortSignal; Angular's HttpClient cancels on unsubscribe), when takeUntil is placed before a flattening or sharing operator (the inner keeps running), or when the notifier completes without emitting (nothing stops).

hooks.clause: stopping a live gate is a takeUntil notifier for every stream it owns

tools.title: Timeouts: timeout and race

transform.reason: Timeout fallback and first-source racing require distinct response and cancellation contracts.

observable: Candidate timelines compare deadline expiry with first-response selection.

tools.definition: Problem: bound the wait. Shape: timeout({first, each, with: () => fallback$, meta}) errors with TimeoutError or switches to a fallback; race([a$, b$]) mirrors whichever source emits first and drops the others. Fails when: race's loser errors before any emission (race errors), when `each` is applied to a stream with legitimate long gaps, or when the fallback hides a dead dependency.

hooks.clause: the loopback request's transport deadline and a status poll's per-request timeout

tools.title: Higher-order observables and flattening

transform.reason: A flattening strategy and an inner-work lifecycle must be chosen before behavior is executable.

observable: Candidate traces compare overlapping, queued, replaced and ignored work.

tools.definition: An observable of observables must be flattened; the four flattening strategies (merge, concat, switch, exhaust) differ only in what happens to the running inner stream when a new outer value arrives.

tools.title: Retry with exponential backoff and jitter

transform.reason: Retrying a source needs failure classes, replay safety and an execution contract.

observable: Candidate traces show increasing waits between transient failures.

tools.definition: Problem: transient failures. Shape: retry({count, delay: (err, n) => timer(Math.min(base * 2 ** n, cap) + random jitter), resetOnSuccess: true}); if the delay notifier completes without emitting, the result completes without error. Fails when: non-retryable errors (validation, 4xx) are retried (rethrow them from the delay function), count is unbounded against a dead endpoint, or retry wraps the outer stream so one retried inner restarts everything.

hooks.clause: resident backoff policy; a status route poll with capped jittered retry

tools.title: Polling: timer + switchMap, or repeat with delay

transform.reason: Periodic loading needs source generation and a chosen fixed or completion-relative cadence.

observable: Candidate timelines compare fixed ticks with waiting after each response.

tools.definition: Problem: periodic refresh. Shape A: timer(0, period).pipe(switchMap(() => load())) polls on a fixed cadence and cancels slow responses. Shape B: load().pipe(repeat({delay: period})) waits for each response before scheduling the next. Add retry({delay}) for failures and takeUntil(stop$). Fails when: fixed cadence overlaps slow responses (prefer B), when polling continues in hidden tabs, or when success and failure should have different cadences.

hooks.clause: the live console caps refresh at once per second; a loopback status poll is shape B with retry

tools.title: Stale-while-revalidate

transform.reason: Stale and fresh results need cache contents, request behavior and a status schema.

observable: Candidate traces retain old data while a replacement request runs.

tools.definition: Problem: show cached data at once and refresh behind it. Shape: cache$.pipe(switchMap(cached => fresh$.pipe(map(toReady), startWith(toStale(cached)), catchError(() => of(toStaleWithError(cached)))))) with a stale/fresh flag in the union. Fails when: a fresh error wipes the shown cache, when stale and fresh look identical to the user, or when revalidation runs on every subscriber (share it).

hooks.clause: the live view keeps the last snapshot without freshness indication; a stale flag in the union is the fix

verified.note: MK (term from HTTP caching RFC 5861; RxJS form unverified); DOTLN

tools.title: Circuit breaker

transform.reason: Breaker states require outcome classification, shared health state and a probe protocol.

observable: Candidate traces show accepted requests, cooldown rejection and limited probes.

tools.definition: Problem: stop hammering a failing dependency. Shape: a shared scan-driven state machine (closed → open after N failures → half-open after a cooldown) gates requests (iif or switchMap on breaker state) and counts outcomes via materialize or catchError. Fails when: breaker state is per-subscriber (must be shared), half-open probes are not rate-limited, or the breaker never records successes (resetOnSuccess analogue).

hooks.clause: resident backoff versus stop-on-host-preparation-failure is a breaker-like policy

tools.title: Heartbeat and liveness detection

transform.reason: Heartbeat generation and peer-health state need a liveness protocol beyond a delivery timeout.

observable: Candidate timelines compare periodic probes with the duration of peer silence.

tools.definition: Problem: detect a silent peer. Shape: timer(0, hb).pipe(switchMap(ping)) for outgoing heartbeats; incoming$.pipe(timeout({each: lease})) treats silence longer than the lease as failure. Fails when: heartbeats mask real failures (the peer answers pings but not work), or when lease and heartbeat periods are too close.

hooks.clause: the skeleton host's one-second heartbeat and five-second lease are this pair

tools.title: Rate limiting: throttle and throttleTime

observable: The first message opens a window and is delivered immediately.
Other arrivals are suppressed, with an optional final message at the window boundary.

tools.definition: Problem: too many events. Shape: throttleTime(ms, scheduler, {leading, trailing}) emits the first value in each window and optionally the trailing one; throttle takes a duration-selector observable. Fails when: the final value matters but trailing is left false (the default), so the last position or keystroke is dropped.

tools.title: auditTime for UI

observable: The first arrival starts a window without immediate delivery.
Only the latest buffered message is delivered when that window ends.

tools.definition: Emit the latest value at the end of each window after a source emission: the right shape for scroll, resize and pointer position where only the latest matters and a bounded cadence is wanted.

tools.title: debounce vs throttle vs audit vs sample vs buffer

transform.reason: The alternatives preserve different events; a concrete survivor and timing rule must be chosen.

observable: Candidate timelines compare which messages survive each timing policy.

tools.definition: Choose by which value survives and when: debounce (last after silence; typeahead), throttle (first per window; clicks), audit (last per window; scroll), sample (latest on a tick; animation), bufferTime (all; batching).

tools.title: Batching: bufferTime and bufferCount

observable: Queued messages are released together when the time window ends or the batch limit is reached.
An empty queue produces no delivery batch.

tools.definition: Problem: coalesce many small events into one write. Shape: events$.pipe(bufferTime(ms, null, maxSize), filter(b => b.length > 0)) or bufferCount(n). Fails when: empty arrays fire each window (filter them), when a partially filled buffer is lost on error or unsubscribe, or when ordering across buffers matters to the consumer.

tools.title: Concurrency limits: mergeMap(project, concurrent)

observable: At most the selected number of deliveries await acknowledgement at once.
Further messages wait until an active delivery frees a slot.

tools.definition: Problem: too many parallel inner streams. Shape: mergeMap(fn, concurrent) runs at most `concurrent` inners and queues the rest; concurrent = 1 behaves like concatMap. Fails when: the queue grows without bound (no back-pressure signal; add buffering or dropping policies), or when a stuck inner holds a slot forever (timeout).

worker fan-out as mergeMap with a bound, not unbounded merge

tools.title: Upstream and downstream ordering

transform.reason: Operator placement needs a subscription graph and teardown propagation contract.

observable: Candidate traces show which inner work survives an outer stop.

tools.definition: Operators earlier in a pipe are upstream of later ones; because each operator function wraps the previous observable, order carries meaning (a takeUntil before a flattening operator does not stop the inner work).
