tools.title: Work queue / pool

observable: Waiting work messages enter delivery as worker slots become free.
The view distinguishes pending, active and acknowledged messages.

tools.definition: A Subject of jobs flattened with mergeMap(run, poolSize) or concatMap, with per-job status reported through materialize or a status union; completion of the queue is a separate signal because the Subject never completes.

tools.title: Pagination and infinite scroll: scan and expand

transform.reason: Pagination needs response links, item identities, accumulation and termination rules.

observable: Candidate traces show page requests and growth of a deduplicated result.

tools.definition: Problem: load pages on demand or until exhausted. Shape: user-driven: loadMore$.pipe(exhaustMap(() => page(next)), scan((all, p) => all.concat(p.items), [])); exhaustive: first$.pipe(expand(res => res.next ? page(res.next) : EMPTY, concurrent)). Fails when: expand lacks a termination branch (never completes), scan accumulates duplicates after a refresh (reset by nesting under a switchMap on the reset trigger), or pages arrive out of order under mergeMap.

verified.note: RX-SRC expand, scan; LRX (gameloop uses expand)

tools.title: Back-pressure is a design choice

transform.reason: Lossless queuing versus lossy compression is a choice, without a selected policy or bound.

observable: Candidate traces compare backlog growth with deliberate message loss.

tools.definition: RxJS has no demand signal from consumer to producer; teams pick lossy handling (throttle, sample, audit, debounce) or lossless handling (buffer, concatMap queue) explicitly per stream.

place.chapter: D4. Flow control, batching and collections

tools.title: Caching the latest: shareReplay(1) with refCount

transform.reason: Replay delivery fits channels, but shared producer identity and reference-counted lifetime are not modeled.

observable: Candidate traces compare cached delivery with starting and stopping the source.

tools.definition: Problem: expensive source, many late subscribers. Shape: source$.pipe(shareReplay({bufferSize: 1, refCount: true})) multicasts and replays the latest; refCount: true disconnects from the source when subscribers drop to zero. Fails when: refCount is false (the default) so the source lives forever (leak; lint no-sharereplay), when an error is replayed to late subscribers, or when the buffer size is omitted (lint no-ignored-replay-buffer).

verified.note: RX-SRC shareReplay (ShareReplayConfig); ESL; ESL-X; KURATA; AID-STREAMS

tools.title: share with reset options

transform.reason: Reset options control shared producer lifetime and identity, which the enum does not model.

observable: Candidate traces show when a completed, failed or idle source restarts.

tools.definition: share({connector, resetOnError, resetOnComplete, resetOnRefCountZero}) replaces the multicast/publish/refCount family; each reset flag decides whether the shared stream goes cold again (retryable, repeatable, or disconnect-when-idle), and each accepts a notifier factory for delayed resets.

tools.title: Subject variants as caches
tools.definition: BehaviorSubject holds a current value for late subscribers; ReplaySubject(n, windowTime) replays a bounded, time-limited history; AsyncSubject emits only the last value on completion; Subject<void> signals that something happened.

tools.title: Reference counting

transform.reason: Starting and stopping a producer from subscriber counts needs a source-lifetime model.

observable: Candidate traces show producer activation on the first receiver and cleanup on the last.

tools.definition: A multicast starts its source when the first subscriber arrives and stops when the last leaves; the modern spelling is share's resetOnRefCountZero or shareReplay's refCount flag.

tools.title: Progress stream: materialize + scan + startWith

transform.reason: Notification-to-progress folding needs a progress state and reducer.

observable: Candidate views show advances, final completion and failure as retained state.

tools.definition: Problem: show progress of long work without the stream dying on failure. Shape: work$.pipe(materialize(), scan(toProgress, initial), startWith(initial)) turns next, error and complete into values so the UI shows done/total, completion and failure as data. Fails when: the fold forgets the complete notification (never shows finished), or the UI never receives the initial state.

hooks.clause: a gate's progress UI: tasks done/total, verdict and failure from one folded stream

tools.title: Loading flag via startWith and finalize

transform.reason: Loading indicators require derived UI state and resource finalization callbacks.

observable: Candidate traces show the indicator clearing after completion, failure or cancellation.

tools.definition: loading$ = trigger$.pipe(switchMap(() => load().pipe(map(() => false), startWith(true)))) or tap/finalize around the request; finalize runs on complete, error and unsubscribe, so cancellation also clears the flag.

tools.title: Save indicator

transform.reason: Saving status requires a save operation and a status-state derivation contract.

observable: Candidate traces show pending and confirmed changes without repeated status flicker.

tools.definition: Debounced edits trigger saves; the indicator derives 'saving' then 'saved' from the save stream (concat of status values, switchAll to supersede, distinctUntilChanged to avoid flicker).
